title: SAML delegation, RBAC boundaries, and KMS/HSM evidence acceptance — staged PRD and signoff flow
creator: Ava Martinez
description: This ticket consolidates PRD clarifications, explicit scope decisions, and an itemized signoff checklist for SAML delegation, RBAC role boundaries, and customer KMS/HSM evidence for Private/VPC deployments. It captures agreed trade-offs after the Feb design workshop and defines staged acceptance gates (Dev->Canary->GA) and the artifacts required for audit evidence. The goal is to remove ambiguity around operator vs customer responsibilities, evidence templates, and failure-mode acceptance before shipping the private deploy onboarding flow.
background: Multiple PM and security reviews flagged gaps in: (1) what constitutes pass/fail for SAML assertions and provisioning, (2) RBAC role separation between 'operator' and 'customer-admin', and (3) acceptable KMS/HSM evidence for FIPS/regulated customers. Engineering requested concrete test vectors and machine-readable evidence exports to automate acceptance verification.
scope_in_scope: SAML: assertion lifetime, audience restrictions, replay protection, and SCIM provisioning validation
RBAC: canonical role hierarchy, least-privilege defaults, and change approval workflow for owner-level role grants
KMS/HSM: support for CMEK with HSM-backed keys, key rotation workflow, and signed audit evidence exports
Audit logs: immutable ingest, customer copy/export, retention policy and retention snapshots for 90/365d plans
Signoff artifacts: evidence package templates, automated verification scripts, and human review checklists
scope_out_of_scope: Full multi-tenant HSM provisioning UI (we require operator-run manual provisioning for alpha)
Custom SAML IdP setup automation beyond our documented templates
Cross-cloud KMS federation (deferred to next quarter)
Legal contract language changes — linkage to legal templates is advisory only
acceptance_criteria: SAML: Live test where a customer IdP completes SSO and SCIM provisioning; artifacts include SAML assertion logs with audience and nonce, and SCIM user creation events (pass/fail matrix provided).
RBAC: Demonstration of role grant request -> approval workflow; unit + e2e tests proving no privilege escalation path from 'developer' to 'customer-admin' in 1000 randomized role-change scenarios.
KMS/HSM: Evidence package showing a CMEK-backed model serving run where key usage logs, HSM attestation, and a successful key rotation without downtime are captured and verifiable.
Audit logs: Exported immutable archive for a 30-day window containing request IDs, subject identities, key identifiers, and signed digests; automated verifier must validate digest integrity.
Operator responsibilities: Documentation and runbook present for emergency key-escrow usage and revocation proving a tested, documented sequence that produces audit evidence.
Security review: External security review (3rd-party) signoff OR documented compensating controls if an external review is deferred.
Regression criteria: No high or critical SLO regressions in latency or error-rate in dedicated/private test clusters after enabling SAML/KMS integration for 72h Canary.
Traceability: Every acceptance artifact links to one or more automated test outcomes, or to a named reviewer with signoff date.

test_plan: Unit tests: RBAC policy evaluation matrix coverage >= 95% for critical paths
Integration: End-to-end SAML login + SCIM provisioning against Okta test tenant (automated), repeated 10x with varying clock skews
Chaos: Simulate KMS latency and HSM attestation failure; verify graceful fallback and documented operator steps
Performance: Canary run with 48h steady-state verification and no >1% spike in 99th latency
Audit verification: Run verifier script against 30-day archive and validate signed manifest integrity
rollout_plan: Three-phase rollout: (1) internal dogfood + security review (2) invited-customer Canary (select customers with audit requirements) for 2 weeks, (3) gradual GA. Each phase requires completion of its signoff checklist items before progressing. Emergency rollback uses documented operator script to strip CMEK from a project and resume using platform-managed keys; rollback produces its own evidence package for audit.
